status: Final Step 1 source coverage for the Four-Dimensional SCFT Data and Duality Frontier. All seven source entries were full-text fetched and inspected; source-fetch-check confirms 7/7 fetch-verified and resolved, with zero documented drops. Per-item support, limitations, fetch stamps, and the unused D'Hoker–Phong retrieval failure are recorded below.

source_review.read_extent: Read the full lecture-note PDF and inspected the four-dimensional supersymmetry algebra and representations in §§2.2–2.4, the N=4 field content in §4.4.2, and the N=1 superconformal algebra and chiral-dimension bound in §6.4.2.
source_review.supports: The selected N=4 field multiplets, the distinction between a conformal fixed point and a Lagrangian model, the N=1 subalgebra used for the index, and the stated scalar chiral-primary bound.
source_review.limitations: The notes explicitly do not prove the general superconformal unitarity classification; the cited N=4 field-content discussion does not establish S-duality or a rigorous continuum construction.

source_review.read_extent: Read §6.4.2's displayed N=1 superconformal anticommutators and scalar chiral-dimension relation.
source_review.supports: Independent convention check for the algebraic scalar bound; the item proves its conditional norm inequality locally.
source_review.limitations: The notes state the representation-theoretic result without deriving it; no proof is imported.

sources.title: Justin Kinney, Juan Maldacena, Shiraz Minwalla, and Suvrat Raju, An Index for 4 Dimensional Super Conformal Theories
sources.locator: §3, printed pp. 12–15, especially equations (3.1)–(3.3); §4.1, printed pp. 16–19, for the N=4 Yang–Mills index calculation and its regulator/setup qualifications.

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved and read the full 56-page PDF; inspected the chosen supercharge, positive anticommutator, commuting charge insertions, trace definition, cancellation of positive-Delta states, and the N=4 index calculation in §4.1.
source_review.supports: The precise radial-quantization trace convention and the distinction between a protected superconformal index and an ungraded partition function over BPS states.
source_review.limitations: The paper's N=4 weak-coupling calculation and large-N comparison are not a construction of the continuum QFT; the local theorem proves only conditional trace cancellation under explicit operator and trace-class assumptions.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete cancellation argument in §3 from the positive supercharge anticommutator through the trace formula (3.3).
source_review.supports: The chosen Q-pair mechanism and commuting-charge requirement; the local proof supplies its operator-domain and trace-class hypotheses explicitly.
source_review.limitations: The source's representation-theoretic argument does not remove the need for the local theorem's explicit spectral decomposition and trace assumptions.

source_review.read_extent: Read §3, including equation (3.1), for the positive anticommutator of the chosen supercharge and its scalar-primary consequence in the specified radial convention.
source_review.supports: The selected radial supercharge normalization used in the scalar-primary norm proof.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem derives the norm inequality from its exact current algebra interface; no continuum representation is constructed.

source_review.read_extent: Read §3's cancellation of paired positive-Delta states.
source_review.supports: The interpretation of the finite two-state calculation as the elementary index-cancellation mechanism.
source_review.limitations: The two-state item is an explicitly finite supercharge model and is not asserted to be a full four-dimensional SCFT.

sources.title: Anton Kapustin and Edward Witten, Electric-Magnetic Duality and the Geometric Langlands Program
sources.kind: primary paper and full lecture-style treatment
sources.locator: §2.1–2.2, printed pp. 7–12: N=4 field content, trace/coupling normalization, tau parameter, S-duality status, and dual-group qualification.

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved the complete 231-page paper and read §2.1–2.2, including the ten-dimensional reduction, four-dimensional N=4 field content, tau normalization, and the authors' explicit description of S-duality as a conjecture.
source_review.supports: The source-qualified coupling transformation and the requirement to distinguish the Lie algebra, global gauge group, and Langlands-dual theory.
source_review.limitations: The paper is about a topological twist and its consequences; its S-duality input remains a physical conjecture and is not a proof of the untwisted continuum theory.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2's simply-laced S-transformation and its warning that global form and flux sectors refine the duality statement.
source_review.supports: The source-reported duality map used to interpret the explicitly derived finite line-charge permutation.
source_review.limitations: The example proves the finite charge-lattice calculation only; it does not prove quantum equivalence.

sources.title: Ofer Aharony, Nathan Seiberg, and Yuji Tachikawa, Reading between the Lines of Four-Dimensional Gauge Theories
sources.locator: §§1.1–1.2, printed pp. 2–5, and §2.4, printed pp. 17–18: SU(2)/SO(3) line spectra and S/T transformations.

source_review.read_extent: Retrieved and inspected the complete 52-page PDF; read the discussion of global gauge group, Wilson/'t Hooft line charges, the three su(2) theories, and the N=4 S-duality action on line spectra.
source_review.supports: The finite charge-lattice conventions and the fact that S-duality permutes theories with different global forms or discrete theta data.
source_review.limitations: The paper analyzes line-operator consistency and duality maps; it does not prove the full quantum equivalence conjecture.

source_review.read_extent: Read all of §§1.1–1.2 and §2.4, including the Dirac locality pairing and the explicit SU(2), SO(3)+, and SO(3)- charge classes.
source_review.supports: The source-reported classification against which the local mod-2 isotropy and S/T permutation proof is checked.
source_review.limitations: The local example proves the finite arithmetic; no confinement law or S-duality equivalence is deduced from the diagram.

source_review.limitations: The finite example is not the N=4 gauge-theory computation and has no continuum or empirical content.

source_review.read_extent: Read §4.1's N=4 superconformal-letter representation and its stated scope.
source_review.supports: Context for treating a chiral composite as a protected-sector example in the selected N=4 field content.
source_review.limitations: The example explicitly assumes the named composite is a nonzero scalar chiral primary; the source is not used to prove that existence assumption.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected §§2.2–2.3 and §6.4.2 for the unitary supercharge representation and graded-index context.
source_review.supports: Independent lecture-note context for interpreting the explicit finite two-state supercharge pair.
source_review.limitations: The finite matrices and trace are computed locally; this source does not claim the toy pair realizes a full SCFT.

source_review.read_extent: Read the superalgebra representation discussion and the N=1 chiral scaling-dimension relation.
source_review.supports: An independent check of the chiral-primary conclusion; the item proves the conditional bound locally.
source_review.limitations: No existence of a continuum SU(2) SCFT is established by the example.
